GAP [1]: The mechanism by which the AcCoA-NLRX1 axis regulates KRAS activity and promotes drug resistance is unknown, and understanding this process is crucial for developing strategies to overcome resistance to KRAS inhibitors.
GAP [2]: No study has tested whether USP7 interacts with the KRAS-MEK pathway under conditions of KRAS inhibition, and characterizing this interaction could reveal new targets for therapy.
GAP [3]: It is unclear whether the mitophagy response acts upstream or downstream of the KRAS signaling pathways in promoting drug resistance, and resolving this question could inform the development of mitophagy-targeting therapies.
GAP [4]: The causal path from KRAS G12C inhibitors to drug resistance via secondary KRAS mutations is missing experimental validation of the intermediate steps, and understanding these steps could help predict and prevent resistance.
GAP [5]: The mechanism by which redundancies within the KRAS signaling pathways contribute to cross-talk between these pathways and promote drug resistance is unknown, and elucidating this mechanism could reveal new opportunities for targeted therapies.
